QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_45

question.text: In SROI, monetisation of an intangible outcome (e.g., increased confidence in a woman-entrepreneur) is typically done via:

answer.text: Financial proxies — using observable market prices that approximate the value of the intangible (e.g., cost of counselling services, wage premium, willingness-to-pay surveys)
Listing the outcome as zero because it is intangible
Using the SE's annual turnover as the proxy

explanation.text: The Logic: Intangible outcomes are monetised using financial proxies — observable market prices or stated-preference values that approximate the outcome's value. Examples: cost of equivalent training, wage premium post-training, willingness-to-pay studies, avoided healthcare cost. Each proxy source must be disclosed and sensitivity-tested. The Trap: Inventing values or marking zero are both unacceptable. SE turnover is unrelated to beneficiary outcome value. Cross-Exam Context: V-A Distributor and X-A IA discuss proxy values for private-equity valuation; XXIII applies the same principle to social outcome monetisation. Assessor's Pro-Tip: List proxy sources with a tier (tier-1: published wage data; tier-2: comparable NGO cost; tier-3: stakeholder WTP). Heavier reliance on tier-3 needs bigger sensitivity discussion in the SIR.
